proof_summary: The identity \(2D=2(n-1)(n-3)!+(n^2-2)\sum_{j<n-3}j!\), together with Legendre’s bound, shows that if an odd prime power \(p^j\) survives the gcd quotient then \(p^{\lfloor(n-3)/p\rfloor+j}\mid n^2-2\). If the quotient were composite, its first two prime factors (with parity and congruences excluding 2 and 3) would, whether equal or distinct, force a divisor of \(n^2-2\) at least \(n^2\), contradicting \(n^2-2<n^2\); the lone boundary case is computed directly.
